Assumed mean method. Take \(A = 37.5\) (the class mark of 35-40) and \(d_i = x_i - A\).

| 25-30 | 27.5 | \(-10\) | 20 | \(-200\) |
| 30-35 | 32.5 | \(-5\) | 25 | \(-125\) |
| 35-40 | 37.5 | 0 | 15 | 0 |
| 40-45 | 42.5 | 5 | 10 | 50 |
| 45-50 | 47.5 | 10 | 10 | 100 |
| Total | | | \(\Sigma f_i = 80\) | \(\Sigma f_i d_i = -175\) |

\(\overline{d} = \dfrac{-175}{80} = -2.1875\)

Mean \(= A + \overline{d} = 37.5 - 2.1875 = 35.3125\) (thousand rupees)

\(\therefore\) the mean production of oranges is 35.3125 thousand rupees, that is ₹ 35,312.50.

[Textbook note: the printed key gives ₹ 35310, which is the same answer with the mean first rounded to 35.31 thousand rupees. The exact value is 35.3125 thousand = ₹ 35,312.50.]

\(N = 1000\), \(\therefore \dfrac{N}{2} = 500\). The 500th score lies in the class 10-12, so 10-12 is the median class.

\(L = 10\), \(cf = 150\), \(f = 500\), \(h = 2\)

Median \(= L + \left[\dfrac{\frac{N}{2} - cf}{f}\right] \times h = 10 + \dfrac{500 - 150}{500} \times 2 = 10 + 1.4 = 11.4\)

\(\therefore\) the median of the number of hours worked is 11.4 hours.

The maximum frequency 80 is in the class 4-5, so 4-5 is the modal class.

\(L = 4\), \(h = 1\), \(f_1 = 80\), \(f_0 = 70\), \(f_2 = 60\)

Mode \(= L + \left[\dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2}\right] \times h = 4 + \left[\dfrac{80 - 70}{160 - 70 - 60}\right] \times 1\)

\(= 4 + \dfrac{10}{30} = 4 + 0.33 = 4.33\)

\(\therefore\) the mode of the fat content is 4.33 %.

[Textbook note: the printed key reads "4.33 litre". The value is right, but the unit is not — the mode here is a PERCENTAGE of fat, not a volume; the litres in the table are the milk collected, which is the frequency.]

\(= 60 + 12 = 72\)

\(\therefore\) the mode of the use of electricity is 72 units.

On a frequency polygon the number of students is the \(y\)-coordinate. The largest \(y\)-coordinate on the polygon is 60, at the point (65, 60).

65 is the class mark of the class 60-70.

\(\therefore\) the class 60-70 has the maximum number of students.

The polygon meets the X-axis at \(x = 25\) and at \(x = 95\); at both these points the frequency is 0.

25 is the class mark of the class 20-30 and 95 is the class mark of the class 90-100.

\(\therefore\) the classes 20-30 and 90-100 have zero frequency.

The point whose \(y\)-coordinate is 50 is (55, 50).

The \(x\)-coordinate of a point on a frequency polygon is the class mark of its class.

\(\therefore\) the class-mark of the class having frequency 50 students is 55.

The classes here have width 10, and 85 is the class mark of that class.

If the class is \(a\)-\(b\), then \(\dfrac{a + b}{2} = 85\) and \(b - a = 10\), so \(a = 80\) and \(b = 90\).

\(\therefore\) the lower class limit is 80 and the upper class limit is 90.

The class mark of the class 80-90 is \(\dfrac{80 + 90}{2} = 85\).

The point on the polygon whose \(x\)-coordinate is 85 is (85, 15).

\(\therefore\) there are 15 students in the class 80-90.

Draw a circle of a suitable radius and divide it into five sectors of these central angles.

The central angle of the construction sector is \(72^\circ\) and the total number of workers is 10,000.

Number of workers in construction \(= \dfrac{72}{360} \times 10000 = 2000\)

\(\therefore\) 2000 workers are in the field of construction.

The central angle of the administration sector is \(36^\circ\).

Number of workers in administration \(= \dfrac{36}{360} \times 10000 = 1000\)

\(\therefore\) 1000 workers are working in the administration.

The central angle of the production sector is \(90^\circ\), and the whole circle is \(360^\circ\).

Percentage of workers in production \(= \dfrac{90}{360} \times 100 = 25\)

\(\therefore\) 25 % of the workers are in production.

The central angle of the shares sector is \(60^\circ\) and it stands for ₹ 2000.

Let the total investment be ₹ \(x\). Then \(\dfrac{60}{360} \times x = 2000\)

\(\therefore x = 2000 \times \dfrac{360}{60} = 12000\)

\(\therefore\) the total investment is ₹ 12,000.

The central angle of the "Deposit in bank" sector is \(90^\circ\) and the total investment is ₹ 12,000.

Amount deposited in bank \(= \dfrac{90}{360} \times 12000 = 3000\)

\(\therefore\) ₹ 3000 is deposited in the bank.

Amount in immovable property \(= \dfrac{120}{360} \times 12000 = 4000\)

Amount in mutual fund \(= \dfrac{60}{360} \times 12000 = 2000\)

Difference \(= 4000 - 2000 = 2000\)

\(\therefore\) ₹ 2000 more is invested in immovable property than in mutual fund.

The central angle of the post sector is \(30^\circ\) and the total investment is ₹ 12,000.

Amount invested in post \(= \dfrac{30}{360} \times 12000 = 1000\)

\(\therefore\) ₹ 1000 is invested in post.
